clue.text: Good article about old English author who wrote in German

parts.note: the definite article is 'the'

explanation.surface: A piece about an English writer who, oddly, composed in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is just a link meaning 'concerning'; the pieces run in order G, OE, THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is the most celebrated writer in the German language.

clue.text: Play books set on top of celebrity magazine

indicators.note: in a down answer, the books go above the magazine, so they come first

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
Hello! is a British magazine about celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone stacks books on a copy of a gossip magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: HELLO! is a British weekly celebrity magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy of the jealous Moor of Venice, a stage work.

clue.text: Birds back with first one descending to ground

indicators.text: with first one descending to ground
indicators.note: the opening letter drops down to the bottom of this down light, i.e. moves to the end

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Birds fly back, the leader swooping down to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first one descending to ground' takes the S from the top of STERN to the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender seabirds related to gulls, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Passionate end of the movement, a recital's final bit

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, here of 'the'

parts.note: a motion is a movement
the closing letter of the word recital's, its final bit

explanation.surface: A recital reaches its climactic final movement with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emotional is full of strong feeling, a synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Women's undergarments — they may cause embarrassment

definitions.meaning: baggy knickers once worn by women
blunders or howlers, mistakes that make one blush

explanation.surface: Knickers on show could make anyone blush.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both loose old-fashioned knickers and embarrassing gaffes, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Girl in game ultimately lost

parts.note: bridge is a card game

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word lost

explanation.surface: A girl ends up losing at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a girl's first name, an example of a girl.

clue.text: Broadcasting as one walking very happily?

definitions.meaning: being transmitted on radio or television

explanation.surface: Comparing a live broadcast to someone strolling in bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme going out live is 'on air'; an elated person is said to be walking on air.

clue.text: An item possibly seen when going round the ship

definitions.text: An item possibly seen when going round the ship

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the next piece, enclosing it
possibly says the letters of 'An item' may be arranged another way

parts.note: ships are traditionally referred to as 'she'

explanation.surface: A piece of kit one might spot while touring a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AN ITEM into MAIN-ET, and 'going round' wraps that around SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsheet is the rope controlling the mainsail, an item of rigging found aboard a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Caused irritation, having acted as boss after row

indicators.note: the leadership piece comes after the row

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
to have led is to have been in charge

explanation.surface: A boss who stepped in after an argument annoyed everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, fitting 'irritation', but it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled caused lasting resentment, a synonym of caused irritation.

clue.text: An Irishman too nasty to bring peace and concord?

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are spoilt and messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irishman too unpleasant to make peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing things into harmony produces agreement, so harmonisation is close in sense to peace and concord.

clue.text: Criticising action of quarry workers?

definitions.meaning: quarrymen use explosives to break rock

explanation.surface: Slamming the conduct of men in a quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasting means both harsh criticism and setting off explosive charges, as in a quarry.

clue.text: Sound of Bertrand in speech?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the surname gives a near-identical sound

parts.note: Bertrand Russell was the British philosopher

explanation.surface: Asking what a philosopher sounds like when he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling noise, as of leaves, an example of a sound.

clue.text: US city street in financially favourable situation

indicators.note: the street abbreviation sits inside the favourable situation

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or windfall

explanation.surface: An American city's main street is doing well financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Attacked and broken up?

explanation.surface: Something set upon and smashed to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to demolish someone in argument or contest and to dismantle a machine.

clue.text: Last bits, fancy details — any number to be filled in

indicators.note: the number is put inside the rearranged letters
fancy suggests an elaborate rearrangement of the letters of details

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Finishing touches: ornate details with numbers still to add.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges DETAILS to TAILEDS, and 'to be filled in' slips N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail ends are the final remnants of something, synonymous with last bits.

clue.text: E-learning can be arranged, by and large

indicators.note: the letters of the word may be put in a different order

explanation.surface: Online learning can usually be set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean on the whole or usually, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Holy person with top-class car, one in no hurry

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A saint in a Rolls-Royce, cruising unhurriedly.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller walks at a leisurely pace, someone not rushing.

clue.text: Pirate's funny walk

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters behave oddly and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pirate with a comic gait.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or aimlessly, a kind of walking.

clue.text: Wrecked artist, very old

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly painter, worn out and ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravaged means devastated or severely damaged, a synonym of wrecked.

clue.text: Cake provided by entrance to a university

parts.note: a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Cake handed out at a university gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, a type of cake.

clue.text: Leave a bar, accompanied by university teacher

parts.note: to bar is to ban
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A lecturer and companion walk out of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' tempts as a pub, but it means prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave or desert, a synonym.

clue.text: Word of thanks with poet getting ceremonial tunic

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet thanked and given a ceremonial garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic worn by heralds, bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Lower oneself to be entertained by rude ignoramus

indicators.note: entertained means held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Stooping to be amused by a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend to do something, to lower oneself.

clue.text: Like many a blind Italian

definitions.meaning: a slatted window blind is named after Venice
from the city of Venice in Italy

explanation.surface: A blind Italian man, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blind' looks like sightless, but it is the window covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes slatted window blinds and people from Venice, a city in Italy.

clue.text: Something digital, mostly with quiet beat

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a thumb is a digit
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: An electronic gadget nearly silent in rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests electronics but refers to fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump is to strike heavily, a synonym of beat.

clue.text: On the golf course messing about

definitions.meaning: out on the links, taking part in eighteen holes

explanation.surface: Golfers clowning around on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'playing a round' it means golfing; as one phrase it means fooling about.

clue.text: Doomed fools suffering setback in exploit

parts.note: a deed is an exploit

indicators.note: a setback turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: nits are fools

explanation.surface: Idiots, foiled in their venture, are doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' is the reversal signal here: the fools are read backwards before going inside the exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Destined means fated, synonymous with doomed.

clue.text: Leg gets stuck in bit of wood, running

indicators.note: the leg is put inside the wood

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A leg pierced by a splinter while running.
explanation.definitionFit: Loping means moving with long bounding strides, a style of running.
